_why: ADR 0128's mutation table, re-derived as a set file.
ec_not_resolved and ec_ambiguous both stop at the enzyme name, before BRENDA is asked.
They used to render as 'could not resolve a real KM from BRENDA/KEGG/PubMed'.
ADR 0128 recorded three mutations; the 'revert both branches' one is split into S1/S2 because
the set format mutates one site at a time.
S6 is the ADR's own 'folding the two identity failures into one message': the ec_ambiguous branch
also takes ec_not_resolved, so a misspelt name is told it matched several enzymes. The
`|| ec_not_resolved` goes on the branch placed FIRST; on the later one it is the no-op ADR 0128
already describes.
S3 is NOT the ADR's mutation. The earlier port read 'one message' as one `unresolvedReason` and
wrote that fold instead; it leaves both NOTES intact, and every test asserted on the note, so it
came back NOT CAUGHT. The ADR never graded the field a program branches on; the gap is new, not a
refuted claim. Closed by 'keeps ec_ambiguous and ec_not_resolved as two reasons, not one' in
theStageThatFailed.test.ts. S5 is the same fold through the forwarded-refusal branch, which
passes `reason` through and so has no literal for S3's find string to hit; it was NOT CAUGHT too.
Both verdicts re-measured 2026-10-31 by excluding only that test with vitest -t; every remaining test passed.
S4 is the vacuous-test case: the message's own worked example contains 1.1.1.27/1.1.1.28, so a
test using those passes on prose. The test uses 3.2.1.1/3.2.1.2. Its find string carries the
fallback line because `? ecCandidates.join(", ")` alone also occurs in the ec_mismatch branch;
the fallback text names which branch is meant.
Run:  python3 scripts/mutate.py --set docs/mutations/adr-0128-the-stage-that-failed.json

      note:
